rule: Base images are pinned BY DIGEST, never by tag. A tag is a mutable pointer; a digest is an identity. A tag-only reference anywhere in deploy/compose.yaml or in any deploy/Dockerfile.* must FAIL the register check.
note: This file records what was OBSERVED, not what was expected (Standards Baseline §3). A digest that was not resolved on this host is recorded as unresolved. Writing a plausible-looking digest that nobody verified would be constructing evidence, which is non-waivable.

pins.tag_recorded_why: So a later reader can tell WHICH tag this digest was resolved from at this instant. The tag is provenance; the digest is the identity, and only the digest is used.

pins.requested: a Debian-based CPython 3.11 runtime image, matching the DEV host's CPython 3.11.2 (README.md, requirements.lock)
pins.why_unresolved: No Python base image is present on this host, and resolving a digest requires `docker pull`. That is not within this seat's runtime authorisation: RT-A authorises exactly ONE throwaway PostgreSQL container, and RT-B — building application images — is FORBIDDEN in WO-2 (PBG-RT-010).
pins.how_it_fails_closed: Each Dockerfile declares `ARG CD_PYTHON_BASE` with NO DEFAULT and `FROM ${CD_PYTHON_BASE}`; deploy/compose.yaml passes it as `${CD_PYTHON_BASE:?...}`. `docker build` refuses a blank base name and `docker compose` refuses the unset variable first. There is no tag literal anywhere for a check to have to forgive.
pins.owed_at: WO-3, together with RT-B authorisation. The WO-3 seat resolves the digest with `docker image inspect` after an authorised pull, records the observed value here with the same fields as cd-store-base, and only then builds.
pins.constraint_on_the_resolved_value: MUST be of the form `<name>@sha256:<64 hex>`. A value carrying a tag and no digest, or a digest of the wrong length, must fail the register check.

must_fail_on: an image reference containing ':' as a tag separator and no '@sha256:' digest
a bare image name with no tag and no digest (an implicit ':latest')
a digest that is not exactly 64 lowercase hex characters
a FROM referencing a build argument that HAS a default, because a default is a value nobody re-examined
must_accept: an image reference of the form <name>@sha256:<64 hex>
FROM ${ARG} where ARG is declared with no default AND appears in this file with an explicit status
register_check_contract.must_not_skip: A Dockerfile it cannot parse is a non-zero exit with a stated reason, never a pass and never a skip (PBG-CI-002).
